en.title: Test your knowledge: Climate
en.description: Seven questions about the Climate theme.
en.intro: The typical weather of a place over many years.

questions.question: Check all statements that are true:

options.text: There is more rain during La Niña
El Niño and La Niña affect where rain clouds form

questions.explanation: During La Niña the trade winds get stronger and bring heavier rain, floods and landslides. During El Niño they weaken, and Indonesia gets a drier, longer dry season.

questions.question: The climate in Indonesia is…
questions.explanation: Lombok has a tropical climate with a dry and a wet season.

questions.question: Which of these things can cause tsunamis?
questions.explanation: Large underwater earthquakes push huge amounts of water and create tsunamis, like the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. Wind storms make waves but not tsunamis.

questions.question: What is the Ring of Fire?

options.text: A massive, horseshoe-shaped path in the Pacific Ocean characterised by active volcanoes and frequent earthquakes.
A circle in Indonesia that has a lot of volcanoes.
Irregular weather events that reappear every 3 to 7 years.

questions.explanation: Indonesia sits where several tectonic plates meet. That is why it has more than 120 active volcanoes and frequent earthquakes.

questions.question: Check all statements that are true about ‘the atmosphere’:

options.text: Keeps the planet warm by trapping heat

questions.explanation: The atmosphere gives us oxygen and protects us from strong sunlight. Its greenhouse gases trap part of the sun’s heat, giving an average of 15 °C

questions.question: The temperature of our planet without greenhouse gases would be around?
questions.explanation: With greenhouse gases the average is 15 °C. Without them it would be about −18 °C, and the oceans would be blocks of ice.

questions.question: Check all statements that are true about ‘the atmosphere’:

options.text: We can survive without the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Species that adapt can survive big changes. Many species cannot adapt fast enough today.
